span.label: Three of the best-described food webs in the ecological literature - Ythan estuary, Silwood Park and Little Rock Lake - treated as graphs and subjected to simulated species loss.

span.label: How much of an ecosystem's fragility follows from the shape of its food web rather than from the ecology of the species in it?

span.label: Shows that food webs inherit the robust-yet-fragile signature of scale-free networks, and turns 'keystone species' from a qualitative label into a topological one that can be computed from the web.

span.label: RETRACTED (A JOIN KEY WITH A MEASURED ERROR RATE, RECORDED AS AN IDENTITY) · species —renamed-across-fields→ node
span.note: RETRACTED: A JOIN KEY WITH A MEASURED ERROR RATE, RECORDED AS AN IDENTITY. The edge is `species --renamed-across-fields--> node`. The span: 'Quotation withheld.' Twelve per cent of the nodes are not species - they are genera, families, or aggregated trophic groups - and the authors say so in the same sentence they say the rest are. A `renamed-across-fields` edge says `node` is what this field calls a species, WHICH IS TRUE OF 88 PER CENT OF THEM. This is the sharpest form of the fault because the layer exists to be joined on: a reader joining ecological network nodes to a species list inherits a 12 per cent error and nothing in the edge tells them so. Compare the cell-type labels whose measured self-agreement is 70 per cent - SAME PROBLEM, DIFFERENT DISCIPLINE, AND NEITHER PAPER'S NUMBER SURVIVES INTO THE EDGE THAT USES ITS TERM. — strength of the relation: 1

span.label: Three species-rich food webs display scale-free (power-law) connection distributions — the same topology as many biological/technological networks — making them extremely ROBUST to random species removal but very FRAGILE to selective attacks on the most-connected species.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: This robust-yet-fragile structure bears on biodiversity dynamics, extinction-rate estimates, and the definition of keystone species.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: All three food webs are robust to random species loss: the largest cluster shrinks slowly and secondary extinctions stay near zero.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Directed removal of the most connected species is catastrophic - extinction rates run up to 95 times higher than under random removal.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The scale-free distribution itself is stable under random loss of more than half the species, and collapses after only a few directed removals.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Keystone species are not confined to top predators: in these webs they sit at different trophic levels, and omnivores and parasites are prominent among them.
